paper.title: Mathematics of Herding
paper.abstract: A herd of animals often follows a leader who sets the direction of travel. The leader sometimes turns unexpectedly and the followers reshuffle. Yet the herd regroups itself and stays coherent. Our work aims to understand the herding behavior mathematically. We construct a minimal discrete-time nonequilibrium dynamical system with one-way coupling, and the minimal structure allows an exact analysis. Take the location of each follower in the frame of the leader. The recorded locations form a distribution. The limit of the distribution is the asymptotic spatial measure, whose geometric representation we study. The dynamics of the herd have an exact operator representation with two factors, the operator of a fixed leader-follower pair and the operator of the interaction rules, which reshuffle the pairs. We show that the influence of the leader passes through some follower more than once. As a result, two followers can have reciprocal influence, despite the one-way coupling.

paper.title: Extinction and the global structure of positive equilibria in a ratio-dependent intraguild predation model
paper.abstract: We study an intraguild predation model with ratio-dependent trophic interactions. We first derive sufficient conditions for consumer extinction, total extinction, and global convergence to biologically relevant boundary equilibria. We then turn to coexistence at equilibrium and introduce a biologically motivated coordinate transformation that reduces the positive-equilibrium problem to an explicitly parameterized one-dimensional curve. This reduction enables us to determine how the positive-equilibrium branch connects to boundary equilibria and to classify all of its admissible global geometries. We also discuss the stability of positive equilibria. Numerical examples suggest the presence of periodic and chaotic coexistence, as well as several forms of multiple attractors.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is extinction and equilibrium branches in a biological predation model, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Singular Aubry--Mather Sets for a Homogeneous Single-Input Control System
paper.abstract: We develop an Aubry--Mather theory for the abnormal arcs of a time-minimal single-input affine control system in dimension three with homogeneous cubic drift. We show that the Bonnard--Kupka semi-invariant defining the abnormal locus is a Darboux polynomial of the desingularized singular field, with an explicit cofactor; this gives the invariance of the abnormal locus, a closed formula for the multiplier of its periodic components and, through the antipodal symmetry of the model, their description as lifts of ovals of a real plane quintic. For a compact invariant set of a singular flow we then define a singular Aubry--Mather structure, whose Lagrangian is supported on the graph of the singular field and whose Hamilton--Jacobi equation is linear in the momentum. We prove a duality formula for the critical value, the existence of critical subsolutions strict outside the Aubry set, and the covariance of the structure under time changes. On the abnormal locus the structure selects the periodic components of minimal average cost, governs transverse stability, and exhibits a sharp obstruction to correctors along heteroclinic cycles; for the radial exponent of the homogeneous dynamics, the corrector is the periodic part of the logarithmic radius. An explicit cubic example illustrates the results.

analysis.tldr: The authors develop a singular Aubry-Mather structure for abnormal arcs of a three-dimensional time-minimal affine control system with homogeneous cubic drift.

analysis.main_result: The Bonnard-Kupka semi-invariant is a Darboux polynomial with explicit cofactor, yielding invariance, periodic-component multipliers and a description as lifts of quintic ovals. For compact invariant sets of singular flows, the authors prove critical-value duality, critical subsolutions strict outside the Aubry set and covariance under time changes. On the abnormal locus the structure selects minimal-average-cost periodic components and identifies a corrector obstruction along heteroclinic cycles.

paper.title: Geometric Stability of Dynamical Systems with Self-Generated State-Space Memory
paper.abstract: We develop a geometric stability framework for dynamical systems coupled to memory fields generated by their own state trajectories. Temporal age and state-space displacement enter a nonlinear hereditary force admitting an exact, trajectory-dependent velocity representation. A common velocity-history phase space contains both resting and uniformly translating solutions. We establish global velocity arrest under a uniform geometric memory-gain bound and obtain exact translating-speed balance laws from the full radial imprint. The response slope yields a positive longitudinal exponent on rising-speed branches, while a complementary contraction criterion gives local exponential attraction to selected descending branches in the scalar velocity dynamics, in fading-memory topology. Our principal result is a constructive geometric non-identifiability theorem: two systems with identical nonlinear force operators on an open neighborhood of rest can exhibit sharply different complete-motion behavior at the same subcritical gain. In the first, every admissible trajectory with bounded velocity prehistory comes to rest exponentially; in the second, locally attracting rest coexists with a locally attracting translating branch and an additional spectrally unstable translating branch. The infinite-memory case exhibits exponentially flat force differences, with all finite-order equilibrium derivatives agreeing despite the possibility of distinct global translating families. The framework also yields classical Volterra kernels and distributed-derivative transfer functions by linearization.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is hereditary-force stability and translating branches in memory-coupled systems, without a central entropy, dimension or symbolic component.

paper.title: Global stability of Michaelis-Menten networks
paper.abstract: In a very nice paper, Blanchini, Breda, Giordano and Liessi studied networks of species coupled through Michaelis-Menten interactions. Under standard assumptions of strong connectedness and non-degeneracy, they show that there is a unique equilibrium, which is (locally) asymptotically stable. This note shows that global stability, which was stated there as an open problem, holds as well. In fact, whenever a positive equilibrium exists, it attracts every solution with positive initial condition, with no connectedness or non-degeneracy hypothesis at all; those assumptions are needed only in order to guarantee existence and to cover solutions starting on the boundary of the orthant. The key is to note that the system is contractive with respect to the Thompson part metric.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is global attraction in biochemical interaction networks, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Asymptotics for the number of saddle connections on a slit torus
paper.abstract: We consider a flat torus with a marked line segment $\beta$ and prove linear asymptotics for closed curves on the torus disjoint from the interior of the line segment. We also consider segments that begin and terminate at the end points of $\beta$ whose interiors are disjoint from $\beta$ and prove $L\log L$ asymptotics. In all cases, after quotienting by the growth rate, we compute the constant explicitly, which differs depending on whether or not $\beta$ lies in a periodic direction on the torus. In particular, when $\beta$ lies along a non-periodic trajectory, we show the constant is $2/(|\beta| \zeta(2))$. Moreover, we prove that as a function of the holonomy vector of $\beta$, the constants are continuous at the points where $\beta$ lies in a non-periodic direction.

analysis.relevance_note: Counting trajectories and saddle connections on flat surfaces provides a geometric-dynamical connection.
analysis.tldr: For a flat torus with a marked slit, the authors establish linear closed-curve asymptotics and length-times-log-length asymptotics for specified endpoint connections.
analysis.problem: Count closed curves avoiding the slit interior and segments joining slit endpoints whose interiors avoid the slit.
analysis.main_result: The closed-curve count has linear asymptotics, while the endpoint-segment count has \(L\log L\) asymptotics. Normalized constants are explicit and depend on whether the slit lies in a periodic direction. The abstract gives \(2/(|\beta|\zeta(2))\) in the nonperiodic case and proves continuity of the constants at nonperiodic holonomy vectors.
analysis.context: Flat tori, saddle connections and trajectory counting.

paper.title: A new class of pyramidal central configurations for spatial Newtonian 6-body problems
paper.abstract: While a non-concyclic rhombus can support a central configuration in the planar Newtonian four-body problem, such a configuration cannot serve as the base of a pyramidal central configuration in the spatial five-body problem. In this paper, we establish the existence of a new class of pyramidal central configurations in the spatial Newtonian six-body problem, characterized by a non-concyclic quadrilateral base. This geometric structure distinguishes the new configurations from the known pyramidal central configurations of the spatial five-body problem. We investigate several fundamental properties of these configurations and provide numerical examples illustrating the theoretical results in each case. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this new class of central configurations can be used to construct perverse solutions in three-dimensional space, revealing an additional connection between the geometry of central configurations and the dynamics of the Newtonian $N$-body problem.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is constructing celestial central configurations and perverse solutions, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Unstable entropy for Anosov diffeomorphisms on tori isotopic to Anosov linear maps
paper.abstract: Let $f$ be an Anosov diffeomorphism on the $d$-torus which is strongly partially hyperbolic with expanding center. If $d=3$ or if $f$ is isotopic to its linear part, where the isotopy is contained in the set of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms, we construct systems of strong-unstable and center-stable Margulis measures which are holonomy invariant. As a consequence, we obtain a characterization of measures of maximal unstable entropy in terms of their conditional measures along strong-unstable leaves. Moreover, we show that the unstable topological entropy, a measure of maximal unstable entropy and the Margulis system can be retrieved from the Pollicott-Ruelle spectrum of $f$.

analysis.relevance_note: Maximal unstable entropy and unstable topological entropy are central entropy-theoretic interests.
analysis.tldr: Under the stated torus and isotopy hypotheses, the authors construct holonomy-invariant Margulis systems and characterize measures of maximal unstable entropy.
analysis.problem: Relate unstable entropy, conditional measures and the Pollicott-Ruelle spectrum for strongly partially hyperbolic Anosov maps with expanding center.
analysis.main_result: For an Anosov diffeomorphism on the \(d\)-torus that is strongly partially hyperbolic with expanding center, assume either \(d=3\) or isotopy to the linear part through partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms. Strong-unstable and center-stable holonomy-invariant Margulis systems are constructed. Maximal unstable entropy measures are characterized by strong-unstable conditionals, and unstable topological entropy, a maximizing measure and the Margulis system can be retrieved from the spectrum.
analysis.context: Anosov dynamics, conditional measures and unstable entropy.

paper.title: Analytical Methods for Solving Non-Autonomous Higher-Order Nonlinear Difference Equations
paper.abstract: A system of four-dimensional fifth-order rational difference equations with variable coefficients is considered. The method employed is the well-known Lie symmetry analysis initially developed for differential equations. Linearised symmetry conditions are applied, reduction operators are introduced, functional equations are solved, and symmetry generators are derived. The admitted point symmetries are then used to construct closed-form solutions. This work is a non-autonomous generalisation of autonomous fifth-order rational systems in the literature.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is closed-form solutions of nonlinear difference equations through symmetry reduction, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Physical measures for partially hyperbolic systems with $u$-definite subbundles
paper.abstract: In this paper, we study \(C^{1+\alpha}\) diffeomorphisms of a compact Riemannian manifold \(\mathbf{M}\) with an attracting set \(\Lambda\) admitting a partially hyperbolic splitting \[ T_\Lambda \mathbf{M} = E^u\oplus C_1\oplus\cdots\oplus C_k\oplus E^s. \] We assume that, for every ergodic Gibbs \(u\)-state supported on \(\Lambda\), the Lyapunov exponents along each \(C_i\) are either all positive or all negative. We prove that \(\Lambda\) supports finitely many ergodic hyperbolic SRB measures whose basins cover Lebesgue almost every point of its topological basin. Our approach relies on an empirical basin-covering theorem for attracting sets with dominated splittings. Its proof hinges on a new notion of sliding suffix times, which allows us to synchronize expansion and contraction along a common empirical subsequence.

analysis.relevance_note: Hyperbolic SRB measures, Gibbs unstable states and basin coverage strongly connect to invariant-measure dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove finite hyperbolic SRB-measure basin coverage for partially hyperbolic attracting sets with the stated sign-definiteness of center-subundle exponents.
analysis.problem: Obtain physical-measure finiteness and basin coverage without requiring every center block to have the same exponent sign across all Gibbs unstable states.
analysis.main_result: For a \(C^{1+\alpha}\) diffeomorphism on a compact Riemannian manifold, let an attracting set admit \(E^u\oplus C_1\oplus\cdots\oplus C_k\oplus E^s\). For every ergodic Gibbs \(u\)-state, assume exponents in each \(C_i\) are all positive or all negative. There are finitely many ergodic hyperbolic SRB measures whose basins cover Lebesgue almost every point of the topological basin. Sliding suffix times synchronize expansion and contraction along a common empirical subsequence.
methods: Empirical basin-covering theorem for dominated splittings
analysis.context: Partially hyperbolic attracting sets and physical measures.

paper.title: Interior caustics and rigidity near noncircular ellipses
paper.abstract: We prove local rigidity near every fixed noncircular ellipse from integrable rational caustics in an arbitrary nonempty open rotation interval $I\subset(0,1/2)$. For each fixed $r>11/2$ and bound on the $H^r$ norm of the elliptic graph displacement, every sufficiently $C^1$-small positively curved perturbation admitting such caustics at all rational rotations in $I$ is an ellipse. A fixed $C^6$ bound may replace the Sobolev bound, with $C^1$ smallness retained. The caustic hypothesis can be restricted to a suitably chosen sequence of rational rotations in $I$ with any prescribed rational $\rho_*\in I$ as its unique accumulation point, together with finitely many supplementary rotations in $I$; this family depends only on the reference ellipse, interval, and anchor. The main linear result classifies all real $L^2$ displacements satisfying the constant rational orbit-sum equations throughout $I$ as infinitesimal ellipse deformations, and establishes their analyticity and rational continuation in the complexified boundary parameter. The proof combines analytic continuation and elimination of monodromy with quantitative caustic estimates, finite detection, and Fourier interpolation.

analysis.relevance_note: Rational caustics, orbit-sum equations and local rigidity connect to geometric dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove local rigidity near any fixed noncircular ellipse from rational caustics in any nonempty open rotation interval.
analysis.problem: Determine whether sufficiently small positively curved perturbations admitting the specified integrable caustics must remain ellipses.
analysis.main_result: For \(I\subset(0,1/2)\), fixed \(r>11/2\), and a bound on the \(H^r\) elliptic-graph displacement norm, every sufficiently \(C^1\)-small positively curved perturbation with caustics at all rational rotations in \(I\) is an ellipse. A fixed \(C^6\) bound may replace the Sobolev bound. A chosen rational sequence with prescribed unique rational accumulation point, plus finitely many rotations, suffices. The linear result classifies real \(L^2\) solutions of constant rational orbit-sum equations as infinitesimal ellipse deformations.
methods: Analytic continuation and elimination of monodromy
analysis.context: Caustics and rigidity near elliptic billiard boundaries.

paper.title: Stable Ergodicity for Expanding on Average Partially Hyperbolic Diffeomorphisms with Two-Dimensional Center
paper.abstract: We study a property called expansion on average (EA) defined for any partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism satisfying an unstable center bunching condition. Under a mild set of assumptions, we show that the EA property implies $C^2$-stable ergodicity with respect to volume. Our theorem applies to any conservative, $u$-center bunched, robustly dynamically coherent, partially hyperbolic $C^2$-diffeomorphism with two-dimensional center and one-dimensional unstable bundle, whose action on $E^c$ is close to conservative. We do not assume that the center leaves are compact or that the center foliation has a fibration structure. Our mechanism for ergodicity also does not use accessibility or the existence of a dominated splitting in $E^c$. The EA property is inspired by a condition with the same name defined for IID random dynamical systems on surfaces, and our proofs extend ideas from that setting. The EA property is systematically studied in very recent work of Carrasco-Obata-Saghin-Yang, where they obtain continuity of center Lyapunov exponents, strong positive recurrence, and existence of finitely many SRB measures. With input from our result, they obtain uniqueness of SRB measures for dissipative perturbations of certain EA diffeomorphisms.

analysis.relevance_note: Stable ergodicity in partially hyperbolic dynamics is a substantial ergodic and hyperbolic connection.
analysis.tldr: Expansion on average implies stable ergodicity under the stated conservative partially hyperbolic hypotheses, without requiring accessibility or center domination.
analysis.problem: Establish stable volume ergodicity with two-dimensional center and one-dimensional unstable bundle.
analysis.main_result: The theorem applies to conservative, unstable-center-bunched, robustly dynamically coherent partially hyperbolic \(C^2\) diffeomorphisms with two-dimensional center, one-dimensional unstable bundle and center action close to conservative. Under the stated expansion-on-average assumptions it gives \(C^2\)-stable volume ergodicity. Compact center leaves, a center fibration, accessibility and domination inside the center are not required. The precise expansion-on-average condition: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Extension of ideas from IID random surface dynamics
analysis.context: Stable ergodicity and partially hyperbolic systems.

paper.title: Bounded orbits on homogeneous spaces and bounded geodesics on locally symmetric spaces
paper.abstract: We present a unified approach to proving the following two results: (i) Let $G$ be a Lie group, $\Gamma$ a lattice in $G$, $X=G/\Gamma$, and let $F$ be a one-parameter $\mathrm{Ad}$-diagonalizable subgroup of $G$. Then the set $$ \{x\in X:Fx\text{ is bounded in }X\} $$ is hyperplane absolute winning on $X$. This fully solves a conjecture [Conjecture 7.1]{AGK} of An-Guan-Kleinbock in 2015. (ii) Let $G$ be a connected semisimple Lie group with finite center and without compact factors, $K\leq G$ a maximal compact subgroup, $\Gamma\leq G$ a torsion-free lattice, and $M=K\backslash G/\Gamma$. Then for any $p\in M$, the set $$\{\xi\in S_pM:\gamma(p,\xi)\text{ is bounded in }M\}$$ is hyperplane absolute winning on $S_pM$, where $\gamma(p,\xi)$ denotes the geodesic ray through the base point $p$ in the direction $\xi$. This fully solves a conjecture [Conjecture 1.2]{GW26} of Guan-Wu in 2026.

analysis.relevance_note: Homogeneous group actions and winning sets of bounded orbits are central group-action and geometric interests.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove hyperplane absolute winning for bounded diagonalizable orbits on homogeneous spaces and bounded geodesic directions on locally symmetric spaces.
analysis.problem: Establish winning properties of bounded-orbit and bounded-geodesic sets in the two settings stated in the abstract.
analysis.main_result: For a Lie group \(G\), a lattice \(\Gamma\), and a one-parameter Ad-diagonalizable subgroup \(F\), the points of \(G/\Gamma\) with bounded \(F\)-orbit form a hyperplane absolute winning set. If \(G\) is connected semisimple with finite center and no compact factors, \(K\) is maximal compact and \(\Gamma\) is torsion-free, then at every point of \(K\backslash G/\Gamma\), bounded geodesic-ray directions are hyperplane absolute winning in the unit tangent sphere. The authors state that these solve the two named conjectures.
analysis.context: Homogeneous dynamics, bounded geodesics and winning sets.

paper.title: Exponential loss of memory for random Lasota--Yorke convex maps with local average expansion
paper.abstract: We study i.i.d. random compositions of piecewise convex interval maps whose first branch is full. Uniform expansion is not required, and the maps may have contracting branches. Under a local average expansion condition at the origin, we prove both quenched and annealed exponential loss of memory for initial densities of bounded variation. The proof is based on a coupling argument. As applications, we obtain the quenched almost sure invariance principle and a rate of convergence in the quenched central limit theorem.

analysis.relevance_note: Memory loss and limit laws for random interval dynamics connect to statistical ergodic theory.
analysis.tldr: Local average expansion yields quenched and annealed exponential memory loss for random piecewise convex maps, even with contracting branches.
analysis.problem: Prove statistical stability of initial bounded-variation densities without uniform expansion.
analysis.main_result: For IID random compositions of piecewise convex interval maps with a full first branch, a local average expansion condition at the origin yields quenched and annealed exponential loss of memory for bounded-variation densities. Applications give a quenched almost sure invariance principle and a convergence rate in the quenched central limit theorem. analysis.context: Random interval dynamics and statistical limit laws.

paper.title: Moser Regularization of the CR3BP for Symmetric Orbits: Bifurcation Networks of Lunar Orbits
paper.abstract: We develop a computational framework based on Moser regularization for the analysis of symmetric periodic orbits in the spatial Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP). The formulation enables the numerical continuation of periodic orbit families through collision with either primary, together with the computation of Floquet multipliers and stability indices entirely in regularized coordinates. We further provide a characterization and numerical detection scheme for symmetric periodic collision orbits. We apply this framework to the Earth-Moon CR3BP and uncover bifurcation networks connecting several classical lunar periodic orbit families. Higher-period vertical bifurcations of the planar $L_1$ Lyapunov family generate spatial bridges reconnecting different regions of the same family across its collision with the Earth, while corresponding bifurcations of the $L_2$ Lyapunov family form bridges to planar families associated with retrograde comet orbits. Furthermore, period-multiplying bifurcations of Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) families produce a systematic network connecting to planar prograde and retrograde families. These bifurcation connections in the near-Moon dynamics retain the characteristic organization by covering multiplicities of the corresponding bifurcation network in the limiting Hill problem. Conley-Zehnder indices and related symplectic invariants complement the numerical continuation and provide a topological organization of the results.

analysis.relevance_note: Symplectic invariants give a topological organization of periodic-orbit bifurcations, beyond a purely numerical celestial model.
analysis.tldr: A Moser-regularized computational framework continues symmetric periodic orbit families through collisions and organizes lunar bifurcation networks using symplectic invariants.
analysis.problem: Continue and detect symmetric periodic collision orbits in the spatial circular restricted three-body problem.
analysis.main_result: The framework computes Floquet multipliers and stability indices in regularized coordinates and detects symmetric periodic collision orbits. Earth-Moon computations reveal bridges among Lyapunov, halo and planar families and organization by covering multiplicities. Conley-Zehnder indices and related invariants supplement numerical continuation; the reported network discoveries are computational results.
analysis.context: Celestial periodic orbits and symplectic topology.

paper.title: The second closed geodesic on Finsler manifolds with $\mathbb{Z}_2$ fundamental group
paper.abstract: Let $(M, F)$ be a compact bumpy Finsler manifold with $\pi_1(M)=\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove that there exist at least two distinct non-contractible closed geodesics on $(M, F)$.

analysis.relevance_note: Existence of closed geodesics in prescribed homotopy classes connects geometry and periodic dynamics.
analysis.tldr: Every compact bumpy Finsler manifold with fundamental group of order two has at least two distinct noncontractible closed geodesics.
analysis.problem: Find a second noncontractible closed geodesic under the stated compactness, bumpiness and fundamental-group assumptions.
analysis.main_result: If \((M,F)\) is compact and bumpy and \(\pi_1(M)=\mathbb Z_2\), there are at least two distinct noncontractible closed geodesics. No additional quantitative or methodological information is supplied.
analysis.context: Finsler geometry and closed geodesics.

paper.title: A coupling normal form for reversible center-center Hamiltonians with application to the restricted three-body problem
paper.abstract: Near a reversible center--center equilibrium, the Birkhoff normal form does not describe the families bifurcating from the continued tori, while resonant normal forms capture these bifurcations through a reduced system. For such equilibria with a reflection symmetry, we develop a coupling normal form in which the bifurcating families also appear as tori of action normal forms. Along a selected coupling direction, the first slow harmonic is absorbed into an action-dependent counterterm. We prove that the coupled recursion determines unique even counterterm coefficients, a formal action normal form, and an exact counterterm factorization. The factorization gives a scalar recovery constraint, whose trivial factor corresponds to the Birkhoff normal form. At every finite order, a symmetric pair of bifurcating branches leaves the trivial branch at a critical curve and carries approximately invariant tori and circles with explicit residual estimates. Applied to the spatial circular restricted three-body problem, the construction yields approximate halo orbits and quasi-halo tori.

analysis.relevance_note: Approximately invariant tori and Hamiltonian normal forms connect to geometric dynamics despite the celestial application.
analysis.tldr: The authors develop a coupling normal form near reversible center-center equilibria with reflection symmetry and obtain finite-order bifurcating approximate tori and circles.
analysis.problem: Represent families bifurcating from continued tori through action normal forms.
analysis.main_result: Along a selected coupling direction, a slow harmonic is absorbed into an action-dependent counterterm. The recursion determines unique even counterterm coefficients, a formal action normal form and an exact factorization giving a scalar recovery constraint. At every finite order, symmetric bifurcating branches carry approximately invariant tori and circles with residual estimates. The restricted three-body application yields approximate halo orbits and quasi-halo tori, not an asserted exact persistence result.
analysis.context: Reversible Hamiltonian dynamics and approximate invariant tori.

paper.title: Equidistribution, multipliers, and moving targets in polynomial families
paper.abstract: We study equidistribution of parameters for each of which a polynomial has a cycle with a prescribed moving multiplier in the full critically marked or unicritical polynomial families of a given degree $d>1$. For the full critically marked monic polynomial family $f=(f_\lambda)$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}^{d-1}$, of degree $d$, letting $p_{f,n}^*(\lambda,w)$ be the multiplier polynomial for cycles of formal exact period $n$ having multiplier $w$, we show that for any target sequence $w_n=d^na_n$ satisfying $n^{-1}\log|a_n|\to\ell\in[-\infty,+\infty)$, the averaged current of integration $\nu(n)^{-1}[p_{f,n}^*(\cdot,w_n)=0]$ along the zero divisor of $p_{f,n}^*(\cdot,w_n)$ tends to the $(1,1)$-current $\mathrm{d}\mathrm{d}^c\max\{L_d,\log d+\ell\}$ in the sense of currents on $\mathbb{C}^{d-1}$ as $n\to\infty$, where $L_d$ is the Lyapunov exponent function and $\nu(n)$ is the degree of the $n$th formal exact dynatomic polynomial associated to $f$. We also obtain the corresponding equidistribution theorem for the unicritical family $f_\lambda(z)=z^d+\lambda$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$, of degree $d$. The proof combines thermodynamic formalism, the Eremenko--Levin multiplier bound, and a comparison principle for plurisubharmonic functions, in a partly quantitative manner. A key ingredient is the vanishing of the bifurcation measure on the boundary of every component of the interior of the connectedness locus for the full critically marked family, which we show using Kiwi's study of critical portraits and rational laminations.

analysis.relevance_note: Thermodynamic formalism and Lyapunov-dependent bifurcation currents are explicit central tools and objects.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove parameter equidistribution for moving cycle multipliers in full critically marked and unicritical polynomial families.
analysis.problem: Determine limiting currents of parameter divisors for cycles with prescribed moving multipliers.
analysis.main_result: For the full critically marked monic degree-\(d\) family, \(d>1\), targets \(w_n=d^na_n\) with \(n^{-1}\log|a_n|\to\ell\in[-\infty,+\infty)\) yield normalized divisor currents converging to \(\mathrm{dd}^c\max\{L_d,\log d+\ell\}\). Normalization uses the degree of the formal exact dynatomic polynomial. A corresponding unicritical theorem is proved. The authors also establish vanishing bifurcation measure on every interior-component boundary of the full family’s connectedness locus.
methods: Kiwi’s critical portraits and rational laminations
analysis.context: Polynomial parameter dynamics and bifurcation measures.

paper.title: Expanding on Average Diffeomorphisms
paper.abstract: We study the statistical properties of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms with a two-dimensional center exhibiting mixed behavior, without assuming a dominated splitting inside the center. We introduce the notion of an expanding on average for partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism and, under a center jacobian assumption, we prove the existence of finitely many ergodic hyperbolic SRB measures, and show the strong positive recurrence property, which implies that each SRB measure, up to a period, satisfies exponential decay of correlations, among other strong statistical laws. We apply our results to several examples.

Each SRB measure then has exponential decay of correlations up to a period, among other laws. The precise expansion and Jacobian assumptions: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Partially hyperbolic dynamics and SRB statistics.

paper.title: On the Hausdorff dimension of oscillatory motions in three-body problems
paper.abstract: We show that for the Sitnikov example and for the restricted planar circular 3-body problem the set of oscillatory motions often has maximal Hausdorff dimension. Also, we construct Newhouse domains for both problems.
