paper.title: When vector abundance constrains vector-borne transmission: inside epidemic dynamics within a prescribed population
paper.abstract: The global burden of vector-borne diseases continues to rise, presenting escalating challenges to public health and agricultural systems. Their expanding geographic range and associated impacts underscore the need for tools to project disease dynamics and evaluate interventions. Mechanistic compartmental host--vector models provide such a framework by explicitly representing transmission processes. However, while these models often couple vector population dynamics with infection spread, the inherent complexity of vector demographic processes calls for a more modular approach. In this study, we consider the setting in which the total vector abundance is an externally-prescribed input to a general vector-mediated transmission model. Our objectives are threefold: (i) to provide theoretical guarantees for ensuring consistency between the prescribed total vector abundance and the dynamics of the model compartments, (ii) to characterize model properties related to the local reproduction index (informing extinction or emergence near the time of introduction) and the inter-seasonal propagation, and (iii) to derive insights for diseases transmitted by Aedes albopictus in mainland France. We apply this framework by feeding the epidemiological model with vector-abundance data obtained either from entomological surveillance systems or from an external detailed population dynamic model. Moreover, epidemiological national surveillance data are used to estimate the transmission parameter. Based on this, we derive conditions for emergence and extinction, and show how the extent of the epidemic depends on introduction timing, transmission rate, and susceptible population density. Taken together, these results highlight the value of generating and leveraging entomological surveillance data as well as their model-based counterparts when observations are unavailable (which is particularly relevant in the context of global warming and for the evaluation of vector-control strategies). Overall, we establish a refined framework integrating such data or forecast into compartmental models, with strong potential for a wide range of applications in animal, human or plant health.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is epidemiological modeling with prescribed vector abundance, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Complex Analytic Structure of Hybrid Classes of Generalized Polynomial-like Mappings
paper.abstract: In this paper, we study hybrid classes of generalized polynomial-like mappings. We show that locally they are complex analytic submanifolds with finite codimension equal to the total order of critical points in the filled Julia set (counting multiplicity).

analysis.relevance_note: Hybrid classes and filled Julia sets give a structural connection to complex dynamics.
analysis.tldr: Hybrid classes of generalized polynomial-like mappings are locally complex analytic submanifolds of explicitly specified finite codimension.
analysis.problem: Describe the local analytic structure of hybrid classes.
analysis.main_result: The codimension equals the total order of critical points in the filled Julia set, counting multiplicity. Further hypotheses, ambient-space details and proof methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Polynomial-like dynamics and hybrid-class geometry.

paper.title: Bernoulli property for skew products of exponentially mixing systems over Anosov bases
paper.abstract: We study $C^{1+\beta}$ skew products over topologically mixing Anosov diffeomorphisms, with fiber dynamics generated by a locally free $\mathbb{R}^k$-action. For a Gibbs measure on the base and a cocycle with a nonzero average, we establish a Bernoulli criterion for ergodic invariant product measures. The fiber hypotheses apply to actions that are exponentially mixing with respect to the SRB measure, as well as volume measures that are almost exponentially mixing with a limit SRB measure. As an application, when the fibers are generated by geodesic flows or Weyl chamber actions, our results reveal a statistical phase transition determined by the drift.

analysis.relevance_note: Gibbs base measures, Bernoulli properties and fiber group actions directly match the measure-theoretic and group-action interests.
analysis.tldr: The authors establish a Bernoulli criterion for invariant product measures of skew products over mixing Anosov bases, under the stated drift and fiber-mixing hypotheses.
analysis.problem: Identify Bernoulli behavior for skew products with fibers generated by locally free actions.
analysis.main_result: For \(C^{1+\beta}\) skew products over topologically mixing Anosov diffeomorphisms, the fibers are generated by a locally free \(\mathbb R^k\)-action. With a Gibbs base measure and nonzero-average cocycle, the criterion applies to ergodic invariant product measures when fiber actions are exponentially mixing for an SRB measure, or volume measures are almost exponentially mixing with a limit SRB measure. Geodesic-flow and Weyl-chamber applications exhibit a drift-dependent statistical phase transition. The full criterion: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Anosov skew products, Gibbs measures and mixing group actions.

paper.title: Local structure of sumsets and projections of self-affine carpets
paper.abstract: We show that if $X$ and $Y$ are self-similar sets in $\mathbb{R}$ with multiplicatively independent contraction ratios, then the Assouad dimension of $X+Y$ is one. As an application, we show that for a large class of self-affine carpets, the Assouad dimension of any non-principal orthogonal projection is one. The latter result is new even for the simplest case of Bedford-McMullen carpets.

analysis.relevance_note: Assouad dimensions of sumsets and projections of self-affine carpets are central fractal-geometric interests.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove full Assouad dimension for the stated self-similar sumsets and non-principal projections of a large class of self-affine carpets.
analysis.problem: Determine local dimensional structure of sums and projected carpets.
analysis.main_result: For self-similar sets \(X,Y\subset\mathbb R\) with multiplicatively independent contraction ratios, the abstract states \(\dim_A(X+Y)=1\). For a large class of self-affine carpets, every non-principal orthogonal projection has Assouad dimension one, including Bedford-McMullen carpets. The precise carpet-class hypotheses: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Fractal sumsets and projections of self-affine carpets.

paper.title: $L^p$-Khinchin sequences and transference principles
paper.abstract: A sequence \((\lambda_n)_{n\ge1}\) of distinct positive integers is called an \(L^p\)-Khinchin sequence, where $1\le p\le\infty$, if $ n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^n f(\lambda_k x) \longrightarrow \int_{\mathbb T}f\,d\mathfrak m $ a.e. $x\in\mathbb T$ for every \(f\in L^p(\mathbb T)\). When $1\le p<\infty$, we characterize the \(L^p\)-Khinchin sequences by a weak $(p,p)$ maximal inequality for the associated averaging operators. We also establish a transference principle reducing the weak $(p,p)$ maximal inequality to weak $(p,p)$ maximal inequalities for three model systems: translation along a lattice path in the infinite direct sum of the semigroup $\mathbb{N}_0$, translation along a lattice path in the infinite direct sum of the group $\mathbb{Z}$ and translation on the circle $\mathbb{T}$. As consequences, we prove that $(2^n+1)_{n\ge1}$, the Fibonacci sequence, sequences of distinct primes and their partial products are \emph{not} $L^p$-Khinchin for any $1\le p<\infty$. We study the special class of multiplicative sequences generated by infinite words and we show that balanced infinite words generate $L^1$-Khinchin sequences, while typical random multiplicative sequences over at least two coprime integers are almost surely not $L^p$-Khinchin for any $1\le p<\infty$. We also obtain a {Conze-type principle} for countably generated semigroup actions on a probability space.

analysis.relevance_note: Symbolic words, multiplicative sequences and semigroup actions centrally connect ergodic averages to the profile.
analysis.tldr: The authors characterize finite-exponent Khinchin sequences by maximal inequalities and prove transference principles with symbolic and random-sequence consequences.
analysis.problem: Characterize sequences for which dilated-function averages converge almost everywhere for every function in the specified integrability class.
analysis.main_result: For \(1\leq p<\infty\), the Khinchin property is equivalent to a weak \((p,p)\) maximal inequality, with transference to three lattice-path or circle models. The sequences \((2^n+1)\), Fibonacci numbers, distinct primes and their partial products fail this property for every finite \(p\). Balanced infinite words generate \(L^1\)-Khinchin multiplicative sequences, whereas typical random multiplicative sequences over at least two coprime integers almost surely fail the finite-exponent property. A Conze-type principle is obtained for countably generated semigroup actions.
methods: Three lattice-path and circle model systems
analysis.context: Ergodic averages, symbolic multiplicative sequences and semigroup actions.

paper.title: Input-to-Output Stability and Consensus Control of Opinion Dynamics on Graph State-Space
paper.abstract: This paper proposes a modeling of opinion dynamics in social systems with evolving structures on the Graph State-Space. It builds upon the Hegselmann-Krause (HK) model with variable influence weights, integrated into a hybrid dynamical systems framework where structural changes (agent addition/removal) are induced by inputs. We establish an Inputto-Output Stability (IOS) result under a strong connectivity assumption, using a nonsmooth Lyapunov function based on the opinion diameter; we show that the consensus expansion is then bounded by the maximal deviation of incoming agents relative to the existing convex hull. Assuming constant influence weights, we propose a consensus control result via agent injection in the social system. The results of this paper initiate, to the best of our knowledge, the analysis of resilience, stability, and control of dynamic systems on Graph State-Space.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is consensus control and input-output stability of opinion models, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Entropy and periodic points in pseudo-Anosov isotopy classes
paper.abstract: Let $f$ be a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus at least two. We prove that, for every $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $g$ isotopic to $f$, the exponential growth rate of the number of nonempty Nielsen classes of its iterates equals $h_{\mathrm{top}}(g)$ if and only if $h_{\mathrm{top}}(g)=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$. Thus Nielsen growth captures the full entropy precisely for representatives minimizing entropy in their isotopy class. For $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms, $\alpha>0$, we identify this growth rate with the entropy of the global orbit quotient in Fathi's hyperbolic extension and establish Bowen's periodic-point formula for the quotient. We also prove that quotient entropy is upper semicontinuous in the $C^0$ topology throughout the isotopy class and continuous at every $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphism, even under perturbations by arbitrary homeomorphisms in the class.

analysis.relevance_note: Entropy, periodic Nielsen classes and topological orbit quotients are central.
analysis.tldr: Nielsen-class growth captures full entropy exactly for entropy-minimizing smooth representatives of the stated pseudo-Anosov isotopy class.
analysis.problem: Compare periodic Nielsen-class growth with representative and quotient entropy.
analysis.main_result: Let \(f\) be pseudo-Anosov on a closed orientable surface of genus at least two. For every \(C^\infty\) diffeomorphism \(g\) isotopic to \(f\), exponential growth of nonempty Nielsen classes of iterates equals \(h_{\mathrm{top}}(g)\) exactly when \(h_{\mathrm{top}}(g)=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)\). For \(C^{1+\alpha}\) representatives, \(\alpha>0\), this growth equals entropy of the global orbit quotient in Fathi’s hyperbolic extension and satisfies Bowen’s periodic-point formula. Quotient entropy is upper semicontinuous in the uniform topology and continuous at every such differentiable representative, even for homeomorphism perturbations in the class.
methods: Fathi’s hyperbolic extension and global orbit quotient
analysis.context: Surface dynamics, isotopy classes and topological entropy.

paper.title: Pointwise convergence of bilinear ergodic averages for commuting transformations
paper.abstract: Let $(X,\mathcal B,\mu)$ be a probability space and let $S,Q:X\to X$ be commuting probability-preserving transformations. Let $1\leq p,q\leq\infty$ satisfy $1/p+1/q\leq1$. We prove that, for every fixed $F\in L^p(\mu)$ and $G\in L^q(\mu)$, the averages $$ \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N F(S^nx)G(Q^nx) $$ converge almost everywhere as $N\to\infty$. Our proof introduces a new analytic approach that relies on neither the circle method nor characteristic-factor theory. Exploiting the triangular structure arising from commuting transformations, we combine matrix-energy estimates with Gaussian heat-flow arguments to establish pointwise variation inequalities for suitable smooth averages. We then use even and odd Gaussian kernels to recover the convergence of the original averages.

analysis.relevance_note: Pointwise multicorrelation convergence for commuting transformations is a substantial ergodic-theoretic connection.
analysis.tldr: Bilinear averages for two commuting probability-preserving transformations converge almost everywhere in the stated full integrability range.
analysis.problem: Establish pointwise convergence of bilinear ergodic averages for commuting transformations.
analysis.main_result: On a probability space, for commuting probability-preserving \(S,Q\), \(1\leq p,q\leq\infty\), \(1/p+1/q\leq1\), and every fixed \(F\in L^p\), \(G\in L^q\), the averages \(N^{-1}\sum_{n=1}^N F(S^nx)G(Q^nx)\) converge almost everywhere. The approach avoids the circle method and characteristic-factor theory, combining matrix-energy estimates and Gaussian heat flow to prove variation inequalities, then recovering the original averages with even and odd Gaussian kernels.
analysis.context: Pointwise ergodic theory and commuting transformations.

paper.title: Uniformly hyperbolic strictly convex billiards
paper.abstract: Can a strictly convex billiard be ergodic? For the billiard in a suitable intersection of two circles, we establish \emph{uniform} expansion of vectors in an invariant cone family under the return to a well-chosen section. This is the first and most onerous step towards a forthcoming proof of ergodicity (the Chen--Mohr--Zhang--Zhang conjecture) and statistical properties. Together, this appears to be the first time that a strictly convex billiard is shown to be ergodic.

analysis.relevance_note: Uniform hyperbolicity in a strictly convex billiard connects directly to hyperbolic and ergodic dynamics.
analysis.tldr: For a suitable billiard formed by intersecting two circles, the authors prove uniform expansion in an invariant cone family for a chosen return map.
analysis.problem: Establish a hyperbolicity step toward ergodicity of a strictly convex billiard.
analysis.main_result: The proved result is uniform cone expansion under return to a suitable section. The abstract describes it as a first step toward a forthcoming proof of ergodicity and statistical properties; those later results are not treated here as already established. The exact geometric parameter conditions: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Convex billiards and hyperbolic expansion.

paper.title: Effective intrinsic ergodicity and the transport-entropy inequality: a relation and applications
paper.abstract: Effective intrinsic ergodicity (EIE) quantifies how the pressure defect of an invariant measure controls its distance from an equilibrium state. In this paper, we make explicit the connection between the Einsiedler-Kadyrov-Polo (EKP) inequality, which is central to EIE, and the transport-entropy inequality (TEI). We also extend the finite-state transport-entropy inequality of \cite{CMU19} to topologically mixing countable Markov shifts with the Big Images and Preimages (BIP) property, yielding an EIE estimate in Ornstein's $\bar d$-metric that strengthens \cite{Ruh21}. We also establish a local $\frac{1}{2}$-H\"older bound for the map sending a H\"older potential of finite pressure to its Bowen-Gibbs measure, with respect to the uniform norm on potentials and the $\bar d$-metric on measures. This result extends some aspects of Bhullar's continuity theorem \cite{B25}: it applies to proper subshifts, provides an explicit modulus of continuity with respect to the uniform norm, and does not require strong positive recurrence.

analysis.relevance_note: Pressure defects, equilibrium states, Gibbs measures and countable Markov shifts directly match the strongest interests.
analysis.tldr: The authors connect effective intrinsic ergodicity to transport-entropy inequalities and extend a finite-state inequality to mixing countable Markov shifts with BIP.
analysis.problem: Quantify distance to equilibrium through pressure defects and continuity of Gibbs measures under potential perturbation.
analysis.main_result: The countable-shift extension yields effective intrinsic ergodicity in Ornstein’s \(\bar d\)-metric. The map from a Hölder potential of finite pressure to its Bowen-Gibbs measure has a local \(1/2\)-Hölder bound from the uniform potential norm to \(\bar d\). The result applies to proper subshifts, gives an explicit modulus and does not require strong positive recurrence, under the stated topological mixing and Big Images and Preimages setting.
analysis.context: Thermodynamic formalism and quantitative equilibrium stability.

paper.title: Global Dynamics and Periodic-Annulus Bifurcations in a Reversible Quintic Li\'enard System
paper.abstract: We study the global dynamics and bifurcations of the reversible quintic Li\'enard system $\dot{x}=y$, $\dot{y}=a_0x+a_1x^3+a_2x^5+y(b_0x+b_1x^3)$, with $a_2\ne0$. In the original five-parameter space we treat both signs of $a_2$ and determine all global phase-portrait types on the Poincar\'e disc with one, three, or five finite equilibria. The analysis covers generic and generalized pitchfork, saddle-node, Bogdanov--Takens, and Hopf bifurcations; nilpotent and Hamiltonian degeneracies; bifurcations at infinity; and homoclinic, heteroclinic, limit-cycle-breaking, and periodic-annulus-breaking transitions. For a parameterized class of generalized polynomial Li\'enard systems whose unique finite equilibrium is the nilpotent origin with exactly one elliptic and one hyperbolic sector we establish a unique critical value of the higher-order damping parameter in the intermediate-degree range, nonexistence of a large-scale periodic annulus in the critical-degree case, and its persistence when the restoring degree dominates. Here large-scale means that the annulus closure meets the boundary of the Poincar\'e disc. In the degree range relevant to the quintic system the critical value gives a large-scale periodic-annulus--homoclinic-orbit-family bifurcation marked by a unique separatrix connection to infinity. For the quintic system with multiple finite equilibria periodic-annulus-breaking bifurcations arise from finite separatrix connections or separatrices reaching equilibria at infinity. Using Poincar\'e compactification, local normal forms, rotated vector fields, and separatrix arguments we describe bifurcation sets algebraically or by uniquely characterized critical functions. We obtain complete fixed-coefficient parameter partitions outside $\Omega_{14}$ and determine the admissible critical-surface configurations and their phase portraits inside it.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is phase portraits and bifurcation partitions of polynomial Liénard systems, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: The moduli space of quasimorphisms on subshifts and its pressure geometry
paper.abstract: We introduce a metric geometry on the space of positive, linearly growing quasimorphisms on a mixing subshift of finite type. Two such quasimorphisms are identified when their homogenizations agree up to multiplicative scaling. The resulting moduli space carries a natural symmetrised Thurston-type metric, defined from the extremal ratios of their periodic orbit lengths. We prove that this is a genuine metric and determine several global features of the resulting space: it is unbounded, separable, incomplete, and has geodesics that are canonically generated by thermodynamic pressure functions. We then describe the endpoints of these geodesics and develop a boundary theory for our moduli space. We apply this theory to metric structures on right-angled Artin and Coxeter groups. In particular we construct isometric embeddings of geometric moduli spaces into our quasimorphism moduli spaces. As a consequence, Manhattan curves for metrics on these groups are $C^1$, with equality cases characterised by rough similarity of the underlying metrics. This provides insights into Manhattan curves in settings where neither classical thermodynamic formalism for H\"older potentials nor Patterson-Sullivan theory apply. The same construction recovers the corresponding results for hyperbolic groups and places these examples within a common dynamical-geometric framework.

analysis.relevance_note: Subshifts of finite type and thermodynamic pressure geometry are central throughout.
analysis.tldr: The authors construct a metric moduli space of positive linearly growing quasimorphisms on a mixing finite-type shift, with pressure-generated geodesics and applications to group metrics.
analysis.problem: Develop metric and boundary geometry for quasimorphisms identified by proportional homogenizations.
analysis.main_result: The symmetrized Thurston-type metric uses extremal periodic-orbit-length ratios and is a genuine metric. The space is unbounded, separable and incomplete, with canonical pressure-generated geodesics and a boundary theory. Applications give isometric embeddings for right-angled Artin and Coxeter group metric structures and \(C^1\) Manhattan curves, with equality cases characterized by rough similarity; hyperbolic-group results are recovered.
analysis.context: Symbolic dynamics, pressure geometry and group metrics.

paper.title: Directional Expansiveness for the chair tiling
paper.abstract: We study directional expansiveness of the chair tiling. We show that for every direction $V$ and every $r>0$, there exist distinct chair tilings that agree on $\mathbb{Z}^2\cap V^r$. Hence the chair tiling has no expansive direction.

analysis.relevance_note: Directional expansiveness of a tiling system is central topological and symbolic dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The chair tiling has no expansive direction.
analysis.problem: Determine directional expansiveness for the chair tiling.
analysis.main_result: For every direction \(V\) and every \(r>0\), distinct chair tilings agree on \(\mathbb Z^2\cap V^r\). Thus no direction is expansive. The detailed construction: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Tiling dynamics and directional expansiveness.

paper.title: An equiregular counterexample to the Sard conjecture for sub-Riemannian endpoint maps
paper.abstract: Lerario, Rizzi and Tiberio disproved the sub-Riemannian Sard conjecture with a rank-two distribution on $\mathbb R^4$, of degree of nonholonomy five at the origin, whose endpoint map from that point has no regular values. Their distribution is neither equiregular nor real-analytic, and the equiregular case has remained open. We construct an equiregular rank-two distribution on an open set diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^9$, with small growth vector $(2,3,5,8,9)$, whose endpoint map from the origin has no regular values. This growth vector is maximal and generic for rank-two distributions in dimension nine, so the failure of the Sard property is not tied to any degeneracy of the growth vector. Singular curves of the Lerario--Rizzi--Tiberio-type structure built from the same coefficient lift, inside the strip where our distribution is defined, to singular curves, and the vertical displacement of a horizontal loop is an explicit strip integral. Realising an open set of vertical displacements by singular loops reduces to a graded moment problem, which we solve with pairs of bumps of opposite winding, an anisotropic rescaling, and an inverse function theorem uniform over infinitely many scales. We also state, with proofs deferred to a planned longer version, two results about our distribution: a description of its abnormal dynamics in the cotangent bundle, which explains the example from a dynamical point of view, and the non-constancy of its Tanaka symbol. The latter motivates an equiregular counterexample in dimension twelve with constant Tanaka symbol (constant nilpotentisation), announced here and to be proved in a separate paper. The longer version will also contain obstructions to real-analytic and lower-dimensional versions, and a transversal variant of the construction, which also leads to a modification of the Lerario--Rizzi--Tiberio counterexample.

analysis.relevance_note: Abnormal curves and endpoint-map geometry have a possible geometric-dynamical connection; several related claims are expressly deferred.
analysis.tldr: The authors construct an equiregular rank-two distribution in dimension nine whose endpoint map from the origin has no regular values.
analysis.problem: Test the sub-Riemannian Sard property in the equiregular setting.
analysis.main_result: The distribution is defined on an open set diffeomorphic to \(\mathbb R^9\), with maximal generic growth vector \((2,3,5,8,9)\). Singular-loop vertical displacements are obtained by a graded moment construction. Descriptions of cotangent abnormal dynamics and nonconstant Tanaka symbol have proofs deferred to a longer version; a dimension-twelve constant-symbol example is announced for separate proof, not established here.
methods: Uniform inverse function theorem across scales
analysis.context: Sub-Riemannian geometry and singular-curve dynamics.

paper.title: Explicit Criteria for Finite-Time Identification in Sparse Primal--Dual Dynamics
paper.abstract: We study when selected coordinates become and remain zero in a finite-dimensional sparse-regression primal--dual flow and its exact full resolvent iteration. Invariant balls centered at \((0,z)\), with \(z\) strictly dual feasible, give computable deadlines without rank assumptions or optimizer knowledge. The certificates may be available at initialization. We determine the smallest invariant radius for the continuous flow within this family. For a prescribed positive feasibility margin, center selection is convex and admits an exact finite conic formulation. We bound the coordinate margins for all centers in this family and give a normalized correlated example attaining the bound. A composite Bregman Lyapunov estimate proves rank-free convergence without primal uniqueness and finite identification under strict dual margins. Under restricted injectivity, the discrete gap-based deadlines multiplied by the step size tend to the continuous bound for fixed data, observed state, and certificate parameters. Numerical experiments assess certificate timing. A noisy weak-form oscillator regression illustrates the difference between fitted and physical support.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is finite-time support identification in sparse optimization dynamics, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Finiteness of Anosov and pseudo-Anosov flows on hyperbolic 3-manifolds
paper.abstract: We show that for any closed hyperbolic 3-manifold $M$, there are only finitely many Anosov or pseudo-Anosov flows on $M$ up to orbit equivalence.

analysis.relevance_note: Finiteness up to orbit equivalence is centrally a topological classification of hyperbolic flows.
analysis.tldr: A closed hyperbolic three-manifold supports only finitely many Anosov or pseudo-Anosov flows up to orbit equivalence.
analysis.problem: Classify how many orbit-equivalence types of these flows can occur on a fixed hyperbolic three-manifold.
analysis.main_result: For any closed hyperbolic three-manifold, the authors prove the stated finiteness up to orbit equivalence. Proof methods and effective bounds: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Topological classification of Anosov and pseudo-Anosov flows.

paper.title: Markoff spectra of Hecke groups
paper.abstract: We study the initial discrete parts of the Markoff spectra of Hecke groups of index $q\ge 5$. Using a digit expansion associated with geodesics and a Perron-type formula, we classify all bi-infinite digit sequences whose Markoff values lie at or below the first accumulation point. We obtain explicit formulas for the discrete spectral values and identify the sequences realizing them, including those attaining the first accumulation point. We also prove that the infinite family of discrete values increases strictly to this point. Our results recover Vulakh's description of the initial discrete spectra through an explicit symbolic approach.

analysis.relevance_note: Bi-infinite symbolic codings of geodesics are central to the spectral classification.
analysis.tldr: The authors classify digit sequences realizing the initial discrete Markoff spectra of Hecke groups of index at least five.
analysis.problem: Identify discrete spectral values and all realizing sequences at or below the first accumulation point.
analysis.main_result: For Hecke index \(q\geq5\), a geodesic digit expansion and Perron-type formula classify all bi-infinite sequences with Markoff values no greater than the first accumulation point. Discrete values and their realizing sequences are explicit, including the accumulation point, and the infinite discrete family increases strictly to it. The actual formulas: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Symbolic geodesic coding and Markoff spectra.

paper.title: Pfaffian Positivity for Convex Kernels and Optimal Matching Bounds
paper.abstract: We show that for all positive, nonincreasing, convex functions $f : (0, \infty) \to (0,\infty)$ and for any collection of $n$ points $x_i \in \mathbb{R}$ with $x_1 < x_2 < \ldots < x_n$ and $n$ even, the Pfaffian of the skew matrix defined by $f(x_j - x_i)$ above the diagonal is positive. More generally, we establish coefficientwise nonnegativity for Pfaffians arising from interval decompositions, which also yields quantitative lower bounds for singly and doubly bordered Pfaffians. Choosing $f(r) = r^{-2}$ proves the three nonvanishing assertions in the conjecture of Albouy and Moeckel. Further, we show that the rainbow bound (the product over the nested matching $\{1,n\}, \{2,n-1\}, \ldots \{n/2, n/2 + 1\}$) is the unique single-matching product that bounds $\mathrm{Pf}(A_f(x))$ below uniformly over $x$ and $f$ positive, nonincreasing, convex.

analysis.relevance_note: The abstract centers on Pfaffian inequalities and matching products, without an explicit connection to the strongest dynamical interests.

paper.title: Adding Heavy-Ball Momentum to Distributed Constrained Optimization for Energy Resource Management Subject to Time-Delays and Quantization
paper.abstract: This paper studies a hybrid discrete-time signed gradient-consensus method with heavy-ball momentum, paired communication delays, and fixed logarithmic quantization. The method preserves the aggregate supply-demand equality at every iteration. For a static connected undirected graph and bounded delays, a Lyapunov-Krasovskii analysis establishes practical stability by isolating the discontinuous quantization error as an additive disturbance and closing a computable invariant-sublevel argument. The resulting ergodic residual bound is quadratic in the quantization resolution, and exact convergence to the smooth penalized equality-constrained optimizer is recovered in the unquantized case. For delay-free unquantized quadratic costs, an exact modal analysis identifies the heavy-ball stability region and optimal parameters, with the predicted rate validated on a fixed sparse network. A reproducible delayed experiment reports all constants and a certificate whose guaranteed steady-state level lies below the reported initialization. A separate mixed generator-battery experiment exercises the signed update directly. Finite smooth penalties approximate, but do not generally enforce, the local box constraints exactly.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is distributed optimization and energy-resource control with delays and quantization, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Lyapunov-Krasovsky Functionals and the Existence of Unbounded Solutions of Functional-Differential Equations of Retarded Type
paper.abstract: In this paper, the concepts of unboundedness and partial unboundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type are introduced. On the basis of the method of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, sufficient conditions for the existence of partially unbounded solutions are obtained. As corollaries, sufficient conditions for the existence of unbounded solutions are obtained.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is unbounded solutions of retarded functional differential equations, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Three Machines Suffice for Local Hardening of Electromechanical Oscillations
paper.abstract: The single-degree-of-freedom swing equation with sinusoidal coupling is locally softening: its oscillation frequency decreases with oscillation level near a stable equilibrium. Nonlinear modal interaction, however, can reverse this trend in multimachine systems. This letter gives a necessary-and-sufficient condition for strict leading-order local hardening, measured with respect to canonical action, in two symmetric three-machine operating-point families with equal or opposite power injections at the equal-inertia machines. An exact two-coordinate reduction expresses the condition in terms of a squared modal-frequency ratio and a dimensionless nonlinear coupling measure. The proof retains the induced mean shift and second harmonic and shows that the companion modal family remains locally softening. The criterion recovers both an equal-inertia hardening example and an exact large-inertia threshold. Coherent aggregation recovers the two-machine softening law, whereas the infinite-bus limit retains two dynamic rotor angles and permits hardening. An exact coherent-group extension preserves the selected periodic family, frequency, and canonical action for every finite machine count greater than two. Thus, three finite-inertia machines are the minimum permitting local hardening in the stated undamped, lossless classical model.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is local hardening in power-system oscillators, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Hodge-Carleman estimates and global attractors for heterogeneous elastic waves with localized damping on Riemannian manifolds
paper.abstract: We study the long-time dynamics of the semilinear Lam\'e system of isotropic elasticity on a compact Riemannian manifold with boundary, for a heterogeneous medium whose density and Lam\'e moduli vary in space, under a frictional dissipation which acts only on an open set $\omega$. The elastic operator is the divergence of the Hooke stress tensor, and the starting point is a structural identity which shows that the dilatation and the vorticity of the displacement satisfy wave equations with the pressure and the shear speeds, respectively, coupled to the displacement only through first-order terms. A single weight function, free of critical points and strictly convex with respect to the two ray metrics of the medium, then serves for the displacement, its dilatation and its vorticity alike, and this Hodge structure yields Carleman estimates for the Lam\'e operator with variable coefficients at two energy levels, provided that $\omega$ contains a neighbourhood of the boundary and that such a weight exists on the undamped region. The hypothesis is fulfilled on every compact manifold with boundary by damping regions of arbitrarily small volume. From these estimates we derive unique continuation for elastic waves with bounded, merely measurable, time-dependent potentials and an internal observability inequality, which in turn yield, for subcritical restoring forces in dimension three, a compact global attractor which coincides with the unstable manifold of the equilibria, has finite fractal dimension and is bounded in $(H^2\cap H^1_0)\times H^1_0$, together with a generalized exponential attractor.

analysis.relevance_note: Finite fractal dimension of a global attractor is an explicit result, so the PDE setting does not exclude it from the dimension profile.
analysis.tldr: Under the stated geometric damping and restoring-force hypotheses, the authors obtain a compact finite-fractal-dimensional attractor for heterogeneous semilinear elasticity.
analysis.problem: Control long-time elastic-wave dynamics with spatially varying coefficients and localized friction.
analysis.main_result: A weight without critical points, strictly convex for both ray metrics, yields two-level Carleman estimates when the damping region contains a boundary neighborhood and the weight exists on the undamped region. These imply unique continuation and observability. For subcritical restoring forces in dimension three, the compact global attractor equals the unstable manifold of equilibria, has finite fractal dimension and is bounded in \((H^2\cap H^1_0)\times H^1_0\); a generalized exponential attractor is also obtained. No numerical dimension bound is given.
analysis.context: Damped elastic waves and fractal-dimensional attractors.

paper.title: Increased-Order Generalized Synchronization in Memristive Neurons: Analytical and Data-Driven Approaches
paper.abstract: We investigate increased-order generalized synchronization between four- and five-dimensional memristive Hindmarsh--Rose neurons, focusing on the selection and stabilization of the synchronization map. An analytical construction combines a prescribed nonlinear map with adaptive control, retaining the memristive switching contribution explicitly in the error dynamics. Lyapunov analysis establishes asymptotic synchronization under uniform strict dissipativity and yields a switching-independent decrease estimate outside an explicit error neighborhood. Numerical simulations exhibit error decay beyond the sufficient convergence conditions. A complementary data-driven construction uses next-generation reservoir computing to learn predictors from uncoupled full-state trajectories and an affine synchronization map through dynamical consistency. The resulting sampled-data controller achieves small residual tracking errors without access to the governing equations. Relative to a reference map within the data-driven framework, the learned map reduces median control effort approximately eightfold while improving tracking accuracy. These results connect synchronization-map selection with conditional convergence guarantees and reduced control requirements.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is neuron synchronization maps, adaptive control and learned tracking, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Free abelian group actions on projective fibered varieties
paper.abstract: Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional normal projective variety of Kodaira dimension $\kappa$ and $G$ an abelian subgroup of automorphisms such that all elements of $G\backslash \{\mathrm{id}\}$ are of positive entropy. Dinh and Sibony showed that $G$ is actually free abelian of rank $\le n-\kappa-1$. In this paper, we show that after replacing $G$ by a finite-index subgroup, there exists a G-Equivariant Minimal Model Program for the pair $(X, G)$ when $\mathrm{rank}(G)=n-\kappa-1$ and $\kappa>0$, and the very general fiber of the final model is a klt Calabi-Yau surface or a $Q$-abelian variety provided that the termination of flips holds in this setting.

analysis.relevance_note: Free abelian automorphism actions with positive entropy are central.
analysis.tldr: The authors obtain an equivariant minimal-model program for maximal-rank positive-entropy abelian actions under the stated Kodaira and flip-termination assumptions.
analysis.problem: Describe projective fibered varieties carrying maximal-rank abelian positive-entropy automorphisms.
analysis.main_result: Let \(X\) be normal projective of dimension \(n\) and Kodaira dimension \(\kappa>0\), and let every nonidentity element of the abelian automorphism subgroup \(G\) have positive entropy. When \(\operatorname{rank}G=n-\kappa-1\), passing to a finite-index subgroup yields a \(G\)-equivariant minimal-model program. Provided flip termination holds in this setting, the very general fiber of the final model is a klt Calabi-Yau surface or a Q-abelian variety.
analysis.context: Algebraic dynamics and positive-entropy abelian actions.

paper.title: The global structure of bi-rotational self-shrinkers
paper.abstract: We describe the global structure of the self-shrinkers of the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{p+q+2}$ invariant under $O(p+1)\times O(q+1)$, without assuming properness or embeddedness. The main tool is a pair of piecewise monotone quantities along the profile curves, in the spirit of Hsiang's analysis of constant mean curvature hypersurfaces. We prove that every such self-shrinker other than the two invariant cylinders intersects both of them transversely, and all of them except the Clifford minimal cone are complete. Apart from those of the cylinders, each end is either asymptotic to a cone or meets both cylinders infinitely many times. Consequently, a complete noncompact example is proper if and only if all its ends are asymptotically conical, and this is equivalent to polynomial volume growth, to finite entropy, and to finitely many intersections with the cylinders. The reduced flow preserves a finite measure, and for almost every initial condition the profile curve is either closed or generates a complete nonproper self-shrinker of infinite entropy. We also bound the winding of the profile curve by its number of cylinder crossings and localize its self-intersections.

analysis.relevance_note: The reduced finite-measure-preserving flow and recurrence give a dynamical connection; the entropy here belongs to mean-curvature geometry.
analysis.tldr: The authors describe bi-rotational self-shrinkers through profile curves and characterize proper noncompact examples by several equivalent geometric properties.
analysis.problem: Classify global profile behavior without assuming properness or embeddedness.
analysis.main_result: For the stated \(O(p+1)\times O(q+1)\)-invariant self-shrinkers in \(\mathbb R^{p+q+2}\), all except the invariant cylinders intersect both cylinders transversely, and all except the Clifford minimal cone are complete. Noncylindrical ends are conical or cross both cylinders infinitely often. For complete noncompact examples, properness, asymptotically conical ends, polynomial volume growth, finite entropy and finitely many cylinder intersections are equivalent. The reduced flow preserves a finite measure; almost every profile is closed or generates a complete nonproper infinite-entropy example.
methods: Piecewise monotone quantities along profile curves
analysis.context: Mean-curvature self-shrinkers and reduced profile dynamics.

paper.title: On the group of automorphisms of the escaping sets of H\'{e}non maps
paper.abstract: In this article, we provide an explicit description of $\operatorname{Aut}_1(I_H^+)$, the group of automorphisms of the escaping set $I_H^+$ of a H\'enon map that induce the identity on its fundamental group. More precisely, for a H\'enon map $H(x,y)=(y,p(y)-\delta x),$ where $p$ is a polynomial of degree $d\geq 2$ and $\delta\neq 0$, we show that $\operatorname{Aut}_1(I_H^+)$ is completely determined by the degree and the coefficients of $p$. Thus, the automorphism group of the escaping set, subject to the prescribed topological constraint, can be explicitly characterized in terms of the underlying H\'enon map.

analysis.relevance_note: Automorphisms constrained by the fundamental group of a dynamical escaping set connect complex dynamics with topology.
analysis.tldr: The authors explicitly describe escaping-set automorphisms of a Hénon map that act trivially on its fundamental group.
analysis.problem: Determine the automorphism group subject to this topological constraint.
analysis.main_result: For \(H(x,y)=(y,p(y)-\delta x)\), with \(\deg p=d\geq2\) and \(\delta\ne0\), the group \(\operatorname{Aut}_1(I_H^+)\) is completely determined by the degree and coefficients of \(p\). The explicit description and proof methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Hénon dynamics, escaping sets and automorphism groups.

paper.title: Lagrangian invariant tori for completely resonant nonlinear Schr{\"o}dinger equations
paper.abstract: We study small solutions of the parameterless nonlinear Schr{\"o}dinger equations on the circle. In this regime, the nonlinearity is perturbative and the system is thus nearly integrable. We prove the persistence, in the presence of nonlinearity, of full-dimensional tori. We justify this denomination by proving that they are Lagrangian in the sense that, although they are not submanifolds (since they are compact), at every point their tangent cone is a Lagrangian subspace. This is the first result of this type for an equation without an infinity of external random parameters. We achieve this by establishing new fine decay and uniformity properties of the amplitude-to-frequency map. This is the main technical novelty of this paper. It allows us to modulate all the frequencies and thus obtain non-resonance conditions without any assumption on the choice of the tangential sites.

analysis.relevance_note: Persistence of invariant tori and nonresonance connect Hamiltonian PDEs to geometric dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove persistence of full-dimensional Lagrangian tori for small solutions of the stated parameterless nonlinear Schrödinger equations on the circle.
analysis.problem: Obtain full-dimensional invariant tori without infinitely many external random parameters.
analysis.main_result: The compact tori are not submanifolds; their tangent cone at every point is a Lagrangian subspace, which justifies the terminology. Fine decay and uniformity of the amplitude-to-frequency map permit modulation of all frequencies and nonresonance without assumptions on tangential-site selection. The exact nonlinearities and quantitative smallness conditions: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Decay and uniformity estimates for the amplitude-to-frequency map
analysis.context: Nearly integrable Hamiltonian PDEs and Lagrangian tori.

paper.title: On the Peak Estimation of Scalar Polynomial Systems via Integrability
paper.abstract: We develop a convergent occupation measure framework for peak estimation of scalar polynomial dynamical systems with no a priori state bound. The key observation is that scalar trajectories satisfy a uniform weighted integrability bound whose exponent precisely compensates for the singularity introduced by polynomial compactification. This yields a finite measure formulation with polynomial data. We establish a superposition principle for the resulting weighted continuity equation, prove no relaxation gap and establish convergence of the associated moment-sum-of-squares hierarchy.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is occupation-measure optimization for peaks of scalar polynomial systems, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Fate of Arnold tongues and canards in Mobius systems with noise
paper.abstract: We consider a class of noisy dynamical systems on the two-dimensional torus whose phase evolution is governed by Mobius transformations. In the deterministic limit, these systems favor phase-locking that is described by the band-gap structure of an associated Schrodinger equation with a periodic potential. We use the Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin method to characterize this structure in the slow-fast limit. Then we show that large-deviation theory describes fluctuations of the finite-time rotation number, whereas weak-noise escape actions determine the exponential scale of rare phase slips. These estimates provide quantitative criteria for metastable phase-locking and melting of Arnold tongues over a prescribed observation time. We derive sufficient conditions for stochastic trajectories to follow prescribed canard segments. With controlled entrance errors, exponential amplification of fluctuations along repelling branches leads to an exponentially small sufficient noise scale for canard persistence in the slow-forcing limit.

analysis.relevance_note: Rotation numbers, phase locking and rare-event estimates give a possible topological and stochastic-dynamical connection.
analysis.tldr: The authors quantify noise-induced phase slips and sufficient canard-persistence conditions for the stated Möbius torus systems.
analysis.problem: Describe the fate of deterministic locking and canard segments under weak noise in a slow-fast regime.
analysis.main_result: The deterministic band-gap structure is analyzed by WKB methods. Large deviations describe finite-time rotation-number fluctuations, while weak-noise escape actions control exponential rare-slip scales and observation-time locking criteria. With controlled entrance errors, repelling-branch amplification gives an exponentially small sufficient noise scale for canard persistence. Precise inequalities and parameter ranges: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Noisy torus dynamics, rotation numbers and canards.

paper.title: Simulation-free approximate Bayesian computation for stochastic reaction networks
paper.abstract: Uncovering stochastic reaction networks from data is central to single-cell biology. Simulation-based inference has evolved into a flexible paradigm for this purpose, circumventing the computational intractability of the likelihood. Notably, approximate Bayesian computation performs this inference by carrying out extensive Gillespie simulations, usually at a high computational cost. Here, we propose a simulation-free approximate Bayesian computation (SFABC) framework that avoids both simulation and explicit likelihood solutions of the network dynamics. Instead, SFABC exploits the Chemical Master Equation to formulate a tractable convex optimization with ensuing constraints, which are then used to accept sampled parameters consistent with the observed data. The resulting posterior approximation comes with theoretical guarantees: it can be tightened systematically, and it provably converges to the exact Bayesian posterior distributions. Using synthetic benchmarks, we show that SFABC matches the accuracy of standard simulation-based algorithms at a substantially reduced computational cost. We then showcase the applicability of SFABC to experimental systems biology by analyzing gene transcription bursting kinetics from snapshot, time-resolved, and cell-cycle-resolved single-cell data.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is Bayesian inference of reaction networks from biological data, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Semiclassical measures for quantized elliptic and parabolic symplectic linear maps of the multidimensional torus
paper.abstract: We study the semiclassical measures associated to the quantum map on the torus obtained by quantizing integer symplectic linear maps, focusing on periodic matrices and certain parabolic matrices. More precisely, we consider the time-one map of the completely integrable flows generated by Hamiltonians of the form H(x, $\xi$) = Q($\xi$)/2 where Q is an integral quadratic form. We prove that the set of semiclassical measures associated to a periodic matrix A coincides with the set of invariant probability measures of A. The semiclassical measures of parabolic matrices on T${}^2$ are explicitly characterized by proving that they have at most three nonzero Fourier coefficients in position. A partial quantum ergodicity statement for parabolic matrices is obtained by proving a sharp bound on the quantum variance and some examples are built in higher dimensions. In particular, starting from T___ there always exist semiclassical measures whose projection on the position has only nonzero Fourier coefficients. Moreover, if Q is isotropic over the rationals, then there exist semiclassical measures whose projection on the position concentrate on some subtori. A link is made with the semiclassical measures of the Laplacian on the torus.

analysis.relevance_note: Semiclassical invariant measures and quantum ergodicity for toral maps connect to invariant-measure dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The authors characterize semiclassical measures for periodic and selected parabolic symplectic integer maps, with a partial quantum-ergodicity result.
analysis.problem: Compare quantum semiclassical measures with invariant probabilities of elliptic and parabolic toral dynamics.
analysis.main_result: For a periodic matrix \(A\), semiclassical measures are exactly its invariant probability measures. For parabolic maps on \(\mathbb T^2\), the position projections have at most three nonzero Fourier coefficients; a sharp variance bound yields partial quantum ergodicity. Rational isotropy of the quadratic Hamiltonian form permits position concentration on some subtori. A higher-dimensional threshold is corrupted as “T___” in the supplied abstract, so no dimension is inferred for that additional example.
analysis.context: Quantized toral maps and semiclassical invariant measures.

paper.title: Data Center Oscillation Isolation and Grid Support: Fundamental Limits and Source-Selective Control
paper.abstract: The grid integration of large data centers poses a growing power-system stability challenge. Rapidly varying computing demand can induce oscillations, while the facilities must provide a prescribed response to grid disturbances. Existing controls address load fluctuations and grid support but do not establish their jointly achievable performance. This paper derives fundamental limits and develops a source-selective controller for simultaneous oscillation isolation and grid support. A coupled closed-loop model gives a condition for distinguishing disturbance sources and reveals a direct isolation-support conflict under grid-import-power feedback alone; additional electrical measurements can remove this pointwise conflict but leave a conditional cross-frequency sensitivity limit. Guided by these limits, we design a local residual-feedback storage controller through convex frequency-domain optimization with stability, isolation, and grid-response constraints across operating points. Tests on a single-generator interconnection and a modified nine-bus network show stronger oscillation isolation than equal-order optimized comparators while meeting the prescribed grid response across operating points.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is data-center grid control and oscillation isolation, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Reeb orbits frequently intersecting a symplectic surface
paper.abstract: Consider a symplectic surface in a three-dimensional contact manifold with boundary on Reeb orbits (periodic orbits of the Reeb vector field). We assume that the rotation numbers of the boundary Reeb orbits satisfy a certain inequality, and we also make a technical assumption that the Reeb vector field has a particular ``nice'' form near the boundary of the surface. We then show that there exist Reeb orbits which intersect the interior of the surface, with a lower bound on the frequency of these intersections in terms of the symplectic area of the surface and the contact volume of the three-manifold. No genericity of the contact form is assumed. As a corollary of the main result, we obtain a generalization of various recent results relating the mean action of periodic orbits to the Calabi invariant for area-preserving surface diffeomorphisms.

analysis.relevance_note: Reeb recurrence, area-preserving maps and orbit-action invariants substantially connect to geometric dynamics.
analysis.tldr: Under specified boundary assumptions, the authors obtain Reeb orbits intersecting a symplectic surface with a lower frequency bound.
analysis.problem: Quantify intersections with a symplectic surface whose boundary consists of Reeb orbits in a three-dimensional contact manifold.
analysis.main_result: Assume an inequality on boundary rotation numbers and a technical nice-form hypothesis for the Reeb field near the surface boundary. Interior-intersecting Reeb orbits exist with a frequency lower bound in terms of surface area and contact volume, without genericity of the contact form. A corollary extends mean-action versus Calabi-invariant results for area-preserving surface maps. The inequality, nice form and bound formula: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Reeb dynamics, symplectic surfaces and orbit action.

paper.title: The Restricted Three-Body Problem as a Perturbed Duffing Equation
paper.abstract: This paper investigates the restricted circular planar three-body problem. We prove that for every negative Jacobi constant of sufficiently large magnitude, the surface of unperturbed parabolic solutions breaks to induce homoclinic tangles for all but at most finitely many mass ratios of primaries. Our approach relies on reformulating the restricted three-body problem as a perturbed Duffing equation by introducing new coordinate transformations. This enables us to capture the order of the singularities involved through a renormalized Duffing Hamiltonian structure, to derive the existence and analytic dependence of the invariant manifolds on the mass ratio of the primaries, and to evaluate the Poincar\'e-Melnikov integral directly through the explicit homoclinic solution of the unperturbed Duffing equation. Compared to existing works, our proof is significantly simpler and more direct. Moreover, the paper is self-contained: we do not rely on McGehee's analysis in \cite{Mc} to justify the applicability of the Poincar\'e-Melnikov method.

analysis.relevance_note: Homoclinic tangles and invariant-manifold splitting are substantial hyperbolic-dynamical connections.
analysis.tldr: For sufficiently large-magnitude negative Jacobi constants, the authors obtain homoclinic tangles in the restricted circular planar three-body problem, with at most finitely many exceptional primary mass ratios.
analysis.problem: Analyze splitting of the surface of unperturbed parabolic solutions.
analysis.main_result: For every sufficiently large-magnitude negative Jacobi constant, the unperturbed parabolic surface breaks into homoclinic tangles for all but at most finitely many primary mass ratios. Coordinate changes yield a perturbed Duffing equation, invariant manifolds depend analytically on mass ratio, and an explicit homoclinic Duffing orbit permits direct Melnikov evaluation. The authors do not rely on McGehee’s analysis to justify the method.
methods: Coordinate transformations to a perturbed Duffing equation
analysis.context: Celestial homoclinic dynamics and separatrix splitting.

paper.title: Topological entropy of nonlinear time-varying systems
paper.abstract: We study the topological entropy of nonlinear time-varying systems. We establish conditions under which entropy is independent of the initial time and derive two general upper bounds based on the matrix measure of the system Jacobian and the spectral abscissa of a Metzler comparison matrix, respectively. A general lower bound is also obtained using the trace of the Jacobian. For interconnected systems, we first derive an upper bound using the matrix measure of an interconnection matrix constructed from the Jacobian blocks. We then establish a new upper bound based on the spectral abscissa of a Metzler comparison matrix, incorporating the interconnection structure through subsystem-wise trajectory-separation analysis. This bound also recovers the two general upper bounds as special cases. All bounds depend on asymptotic properties of the Jacobian over reachable sets or their convex hulls. Simple examples show that either general upper bound may be tighter, while a time-varying Lorenz system illustrates the effects of norm selection and subsystem decomposition.

analysis.relevance_note: Topological entropy is central despite the nonlinear control-system setting.
analysis.tldr: The authors give general and interconnection-sensitive bounds for topological entropy of nonlinear time-varying systems.
analysis.problem: Bound time-varying entropy and determine when it is independent of initial time.
analysis.main_result: Two general upper bounds use a Jacobian matrix measure and a Metzler comparison matrix’s spectral abscissa, while a lower bound uses the Jacobian trace. For interconnections, a block-Jacobian matrix measure gives one upper bound and subsystem trajectory-separation analysis gives another spectral-abscissa bound recovering the general upper bounds. All depend on asymptotic Jacobian properties over reachable sets or their convex hulls. Exact conditions and bound formulas: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Entropy of nonlinear time-varying and interconnected systems.

paper.title: Geodesics in the Deep Linear Network
paper.abstract: We derive a general system of ordinary differential equations and associated explicit solutions in a special case for geodesics between full rank matrices in the deep linear network geometry. In the process, we find horizontal straight lines in the invariant balanced manifold that remain geodesics under Riemannian submersion.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is geodesic equations in deep-linear-network geometry, without a central connection to the strongest dynamical interests.

paper.title: Twisted operator algebras of self-similar groupoid actions on arbitrary graphs
paper.abstract: We study self-similar groupoid actions on arbitrary directed graphs together with $\mathbb{T}$-valued twists that exhaust the second cohomology group of the associated Zappa-Sz\'ep product category. We define and analyse the associated universal, reduced, and essential $C^*$-algebras, along with their Toeplitz versions and core subalgebras. In fact, we develop our theory in the more general setting of $L^P$-operator algebras, where $P\subseteq [1,\infty]$ is any non-empty set of parameters. This includes $C^*$-algebras, $L^p$-operator algebras and symmetrised $L^{p,*}$-operator algebras for $p\in [1,\infty]$, as special cases. We use three complementary approaches: twisted inverse semigroups, twisted ample groupoids, and $C^*$-correspondences. We provide, in terms of the self-similar action, general characterisations of topological freeness, minimality, Hausdorffness, finite non-Hausdorffness, effectiveness, and local contractiveness for the associated ample groupoids. We generalise the classical Cuntz--Krieger Uniqueness and Coburn--Toeplitz Uniqueness Theorems for graph $C^*$-algebras to twisted $L^P$-operator algebras of self-similar groupoid actions. We characterise when the natural inclusions are Cartan, give checkable criteria for simplicity and pure infiniteness of the essential algebras, and discuss when the universal and reduced algebras coincide. We also provide conditions that ensure the singular ideals vanish. Using the groupoid model we show that for any $P\subseteq [1,\infty]$, the $L^P$-operator algebra of a contracting self-similar action is simple if and only if the corresponding Steinberg algebra is simple. Using the Toeplitz-Pimsner model, we prove that for the universal groupoid of any self-similar groupoid action on a row-finite graph, the singular $C^*$-algebraic ideal always vanishes.

analysis.relevance_note: Self-similar groupoid actions and topological dynamical properties are central.
analysis.tldr: The authors develop twisted operator algebras of self-similar groupoid actions on arbitrary directed graphs and characterize numerous groupoid properties.
analysis.problem: Relate self-similar actions, twists and operator-algebra structure in a common framework.
analysis.main_result: The theory includes \(L^P\)-operator algebras for any nonempty \(P\subseteq[1,\infty]\), encompassing the stated C-star and integrability variants. Action-based criteria describe topological freeness, minimality, Hausdorffness, effectiveness and local contractiveness; uniqueness theorems, Cartan criteria and simplicity/pure-infiniteness results follow. For contracting self-similar actions, simplicity is equivalent to simplicity of the corresponding Steinberg algebra. For the universal groupoid of any self-similar action on a row-finite graph, the singular C-star ideal vanishes.
analysis.context: Self-similar groupoid dynamics and operator algebras.

paper.title: Trajectory arclength reveals chaos
paper.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the time-averaged phase space arclength of a trajectory, expressed through a normalized Lagrangian descriptor, as a trajectory-based diagnostic for distinguishing regular and chaotic dynamics. The proposed indicator, $\Omega$, is computed by integrating the equations of motion together with a single scalar arclength-accumulation equation and therefore does not require variational equations, neighboring trajectories, or spatial derivatives of a Lagrangian descriptor field. Using Birkhoff's ergodic theorem together with estimates for quasiperiodic motion and correlation-based arguments for chaotic ergodic dynamics, we show that regular and chaotic trajectories exhibit different finite-time behavior despite the convergence of $\Omega$ in both regimes. For quasiperiodic trajectories with Diophantine frequency vectors, deviations from the limiting average decay as $\mathcal{O}(\tau^{-1})$, whereas sufficiently mixing chaotic dynamics exhibit root-mean-square fluctuations of order $\tau^{-1/2}$ under suitable correlation assumptions. This difference in finite-time convergence and fluctuation scaling provides the theoretical basis for using $\Omega$ to discriminate between the two dynamical regimes. We validate the proposed approach in the H\'enon--Heiles and Fermi--Pasta--Ulam systems, comparing the resulting classification of initial conditions with SALI as a reference chaos indicator. The results support $\Omega$ as a complementary single-trajectory diagnostic for chaos detection and as a practical source of scalar features for the analysis of trajectory ensembles, particularly in settings involving large numbers of trajectories or high-dimensional systems.

analysis.relevance_note: The diagnostic is supported by ergodic and mixing estimates rather than only numerical experiments.
analysis.tldr: A normalized trajectory-arclength diagnostic distinguishes quasiperiodic and sufficiently mixing chaotic motion through different finite-time scaling.
analysis.problem: Detect regular versus chaotic trajectories using one trajectory and one extra scalar accumulation equation.
analysis.main_result: For quasiperiodic trajectories with Diophantine frequencies, deviations from the limiting average are \(O(\tau^{-1})\). For sufficiently mixing chaotic dynamics, root-mean-square fluctuations are of order \(\tau^{-1/2}\) under suitable correlation assumptions. Both regimes have convergence of the indicator. Numerical comparisons with SALI in Hénon-Heiles and Fermi-Pasta-Ulam systems support the diagnostic; the full correlation assumptions are not given.
analysis.context: Ergodic trajectory statistics and chaos diagnostics.

paper.title: A zero-one law for the spectral gap property of pairs in SU(2)
paper.abstract: For $n \ge 2$, Gamburd, Jakobson, and Sarnak [J. Eur. Math. Soc. 1, 51-85 (1999)] conjectured that almost every $n$-tuple in $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ has a spectral gap. Toward this conjecture, Fisher [Int. Math. Res. Not. (2006)] established a zero-one law for $n \ge 3$, but obtained only a partial result for $n=2$. In this paper, we prove that the zero-one law also holds for $n=2$. We also remark that a Baire categorical analogue of this result holds.

analysis.relevance_note: Spectral gaps for compact-group generators provide a substantial connection to group dynamics; the abstract proves a zero-one law rather than almost-sure positivity.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove a zero-one law for the spectral-gap property of pairs in SU(2), and state a Baire-category analogue.
analysis.problem: Extend the known zero-one law for longer tuples to pairs.
analysis.main_result: The zero-one law holds for \(n=2\) in \(\mathrm{SU}(2)\), extending the previously stated result for \(n\geq3\). This does not decide which alternative occurs in the almost-everywhere spectral-gap conjecture. Precise categorical formulation and proof methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Compact-group spectral gaps and zero-one laws.

paper.title: Sofic measures
paper.abstract: Sofic measures, also known as hidden Markov measures, have been extensively studied. In this paper, we survey some equivalent definitions of this notion and improve a bound for deciding whether a sofic measure is~$k$-step Markov. We prove that if an invariant sofic measure with a linear representation of dimension~$n$ is a~$k$-step Markov chain, then~$k$ can be chosen at most equal to~$\binom{n}{2}$ and that this bound is tight for sofic measures over an alphabet of size $3$.

analysis.relevance_note: Sofic measures and finite-step Markov structure are central symbolic-measure topics.
analysis.tldr: The authors survey equivalent definitions of sofic measures and prove a tight bound on their possible finite Markov order.
analysis.problem: Decide whether an invariant hidden Markov measure has finite Markov memory.
analysis.main_result: If an invariant sofic measure with a linear representation of dimension \(n\) is a finite-step Markov chain, its order can be chosen at most \(\binom n2\). This bound is tight for sofic measures on a three-symbol alphabet. The proof method: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Symbolic invariant measures and hidden Markov processes.

paper.title: Odd-even dichotomy in the waveforms of modified Emden oscillators of arbitrary integer power
paper.abstract: Closed-form waveforms of the modified Emden oscillators $\ddot x+(q+2)kx^q\dot x+k^2x^{2q+1}+\omega^2x=0$ of arbitrary natural power $q$, and of their damped $c$-deformed versions, are obtained through a generalized commutative factorization that reduces them to Bernoulli equations. We show that commutative factorizations of Li\'enard equations are gauge-conjugated forms of the nonlocal linearizing transformation of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Kundu and Lakshmanan, the factorization constant being half the difference of the roots of the associated linear oscillator. These oscillators display an odd--even dichotomy: for odd $q$ they are isochronous, with period $2\pi/\omega$ independent of the amplitude, within an explicitly bounded range of the integration constant, while for even $q$ the oscillations decay algebraically, as $t^{-1/q}$. The dichotomy is confirmed by an elliptic polar representation, in which the phase rotates uniformly for every $q$, and, for even $q$, by the Bendixson--Dulac criterion applied to the divergence of the vector field. We present a dissipative Lagrangian of Lurie--Rayleigh type and, for $q=1$, an autonomous Sundman linearization that yields a rational first integral, a Jacobi last multiplier and a non-dissipative Lagrangian; for every $q$, $\omega^2x^2+(\dot x+kx^{q+1})^2$ is a Darboux polynomial providing a global Jacobi last multiplier. Explicit waveforms and phase portraits are given for $q=1,\dots,4$, with and without damping, and a recent application to magnon dynamics in the magnetic semiconductor CrSBr is discussed.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is explicit oscillator waveforms, decay and factorization, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures
paper.abstract: We study the geography of taut foliations on compact $3$-manifolds with toroidal boundary components. The central object of our work is the set of boundary multislopes realized by foliations transverse to a fixed flow on such a manifold. We prove that these sets exhibit remarkable structural properties (rationality, rigidity, and convexity) which motivate the name ziggurats. Our main tool, of independent interest, is a two-way correspondence between foliations and contact structures on $3$-manifolds with boundary: we generalize the Eliashberg-Thurston theorem, which produces pairs of positive and negative contact structures from foliations, and a construction of the first author, which builds foliations from such contact pairs. Using both directions of this correspondence, we bring contact-geometric methods to bear on the architecture of ziggurats.

analysis.relevance_note: Transversality to a fixed flow and foliation topology connect this contact-geometric work to geometric dynamics.
analysis.tldr: Boundary multislopes realized by taut foliations transverse to a fixed flow exhibit rationality, rigidity and convexity.
analysis.problem: Describe the geography of flow-transverse taut foliations on compact three-manifolds with toroidal boundary.
analysis.main_result: The realized boundary-multislope sets, called ziggurats, have the stated structural properties. A two-way correspondence generalizes the production of positive/negative contact pairs from foliations and a reverse construction of foliations from such pairs, allowing contact-geometric methods to analyze these sets. The exact rationality and convexity statements: Not specified in the abstract.

analysis.context: Taut foliations, fixed flows and contact structures.

paper.title: Effective Joint Equidistribution of Subspaces of Bounded Height in Rigid Adelic Spaces
paper.abstract: We prove an effective joint equidistribution theorem for $d$-dimensional $K$-subspaces, $1\le d<n$, of a fixed $n$-dimensional rigid adelic space over a number field $K$. The parameters are the height, the image in the archimedean Grassmannian, and the isometry classes of the subspace and quotient after each is rescaled to height $1$. For bounded Lipschitz test functions, the error term is power-saving with an explicit exponent. As an application, our theorem refines Thunder's asymptotic formula for subspaces of bounded height. We also obtain a power-saving asymptotic for subspaces containing $d$ linearly independent projective points of bounded height, with a leading constant expressed as a moment of the last successive minimum.
